summary: Red team of part 1 of 3 of the area p-adic Hodge theory and p-adic geometry: AdicEtaleGeometry, AdicSpacesPartII, DiamondsAndVStacks, FarguesFontaineDiamonds, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups, PerfectoidQuotients, PerfectoidSpaces and RelativeFarguesFontaine. That is 63 stages, the paper routes of the 32 papers routed into them, and the restructurings touching them (RS-01, RS-02, RS-05, RS-08 and RS-32 accepted; RS-20 needs_changes). The other two parts' roadmaps were read for cross-part duplication. 32 findings: 4 high, 22 medium, 6 low. High: (1) Bhatt–Scholze's perfectoidization of integral algebras and J-almost purity (BS22 §§8.2, 10) are planned nowhere, though P8 and PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S4 follow Hansen–Johansson, whose descent needs them. (2) André's perfectoid Abhyankar lemma is used by two accepted designs, but its only route was rejected. (3) The v-sheaf X^♢ of non-analytic pre-adic spaces (Spd O_E, Spd O_C, Spd(R⁺,R⁺)) is planned nowhere, though the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve, Div^d and geometric Satake need it. (4) The general toroidal-tower Hodge–Tate map (Boxer–Pilloni 4.4.40) is planned in both T6:comparison and S6. Medium findings include: the tilting equivalence is planned by a superseded field-only deformation route; Q4 → A3 is an unnecessary edge that puts derived prismatic cohomology below every diamond; RS-05's R5 links put classical étale sheaves below the diamonds; the Berkovich spectrum is planned twice; RS-05's canonical-compactification owner is implemented nowhere; Div^1 is defined as the wrong object over Perf_Fq; Div^1 properness lacks its six-functor prerequisites; the [ϖ]=0 part of the period domain and Kedlaya's algebraization are unplanned; AI.2 plans Fargues' equivalence from a source that proves only full faithfulness; B_dR⁺ is planned twice; the Hodge-type π_HT is planned twice; Scholze's primitive comparison has no stage its consumers can reach, and its logarithmic version none at all; the BT_1 Hasse invariant's owner is downstream of its users; and shared Part II ids lose a brief.
checked: Every stage of the eight part-1 roadmaps (AdicEtaleGeometry 5, AdicSpacesPartII 8, DiamondsAndVStacks 7, FarguesFontaineDiamonds 6, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups 9, PerfectoidQuotients 7, PerfectoidSpaces 10, RelativeFarguesFontaine 11), in full from data/atlas.json and the per-roadmap extracts, with every stage edge touching them and the roadmap READMEs. Also the Tau Ceti AdicSpaces roadmap text (Layers 0–6), which these roadmaps build on.

The five reviewed decompositions of this part (AdicEtaleGeometry, AdicSpacesPartII, PerfectoidQuotients, PerfectoidSpaces, RelativeFarguesFontaine), with their nodes, links, gaps, coverage and review. For cross-edges, the decompositions of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, AInfCohomology, PadicHodgeTheory, CohomologyComparisons and TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic.

Restructuring proposals: RS-05 in full (71 layers, 62 owners, 454 links, review and the RS-05.md tables), plus RS-01, RS-02, RS-08 and RS-32 (accepted). RS-20 and its two reviews (needs_changes) were read for context only. The review status of every RS file was checked.

Paper routes: all routes of the 32 papers whose route roadmap or parent is one of the eight roadmaps, with their items, briefs and reviews. The routes of other papers were cross-checked where they plan the same mathematics, including the ArcTopologyAndDescent, PerfectoidRamification, DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay, HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, DiamondsAndVStacksIntegralPartII and PerfectoidQuotientsIntegralPerfectoidPartII briefs. research/blueprint/make_queue.py (accepted_routes and design-job assembly) was read.

Cross-part stage texts: PrismaticCohomology, AInfCohomology, DerivedDeRhamCohomology, PadicHodgeTheory, CohomologyComparisons, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, DiamondEtaleCohomology, DiamondSixOperations, PerfectoidShimuraVarieties, TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory and PhiGammaModules. Also the cross-area stages BunGAndNewtonStrata, GeometricSatakeAndFusion, HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas, VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories, IgusaVarieties, TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure, OverconvergentAutomorphicForms, ShimuraCompactifications, HilbertModularVarieties, AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.3 and EndoscopicTransfer ET.6/ET.6a.

Graph checks: reachability and cycle tests over all 3508 atlas stageEdges, with and without the links of every accepted RS, for every edge claim and proposed edge. Every proposed edge is acyclic. One candidate fix, P8 → CP.3, was found to close a cycle and was replaced by an early stage.

Pinned libraries (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474): a declaration index and source greps for perfectoid, tilt/untilt, PreTilt, fontaineTheta, BDeRham, almost mathematics, δ-rings and prisms, Spd, v-sheaves, diamonds, Berkovich spectrum (MulRingSeminorm, T2Quotient), Huber rings and Spa, the pro-étale site, the Hodge–Tate map, canonical subgroups, the Hasse invariant, p-divisible groups and the primitive comparison. Mathlib has PreTilt, Tilt (field), fontaineTheta and BDeRham but no perfectoid predicate. Tau Ceti has Huber rings, Spa and the affinoid analytic locus but nothing perfectoid.

Public sources read (accessed 2026-09-24): Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms (arXiv:1905.08229v4) §§1, 7, 8, 10; Hansen–Johansson arXiv:2011.03951v2 §5; Scholze, torsion paper (Annals 182, 2015) §§II.2, III.2.3; Kedlaya–Liu arXiv:1301.0792v5 §3.6; Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lectures, Lectures 6, 13, 14, 18; Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds (2026 manuscript and arXiv:1709.07343v4), §§5–6, 13, 15, 18, 24; Fargues–Scholze arXiv:2102.13459 (v1 and v4) Chapters II, IV, VI; Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze arXiv:1602.03148v3 §4.3; Kedlaya arXiv:1602.09016v5 §3; Boxer–Pilloni arXiv:2110.10251v1 §4.4; BCGP arXiv:2502.20645v1 §4.4; Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu arXiv:1912.09836 (abstract).

findings.where: PerfectoidSpaces:P8; PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S4 (and S2); PerfectoidQuotients:Q4; PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22 routes 2–3 (unreviewed)
findings.claim: P8 and S4 follow Hansen–Johansson §5, whose descent argument needs Bhatt–Scholze's theorem that every integral algebra over a perfectoid ring has a universal perfectoidization (BS22 Thm 1.17(1) = Thm 10.11). Its proof uses BS22 §8.2 (the arc-sheaf description of perfectoidization) and §§10.1–10.2 (almost mathematics for an arbitrary ideal J and J-almost purity 10.9). No layer plans these: Q2 and Q4 stop at semiperfectoid quotients (BS22 7.3–7.4). The only proposal, the unreviewed BS22 extraction, routes them into Q2/Q4 and P0/P3, which is impossible without cycles.
findings.evidence: P8: 'For Hodge-type closed embeddings, combine the tower's closed loci with Q4's universal perfectoidization … Source: Hansen–Johansson §5 and ECD 5.8.' HJ arXiv:2011.03951v2, Lemma 5.10 (p. 32): 'Since R⁺ is integral perfectoid and R⁺→S⁺ is an integral ring map, [BS19, Theorem 1.16(1)] guarantees the existence of an integral perfectoid S⁺-algebra S⁺_perfd such that any map from S⁺ to an integral perfectoid ring factors uniquely'; Prop. 5.14 (p. 34): 'relies crucially on the perfectoidization theorem of Bhatt-Scholze recalled in Lemma 5.10'. BS22 arXiv:1905.08229v4 p. 9 (Thm 1.17(1) = Thm 10.11) and p. 81: 'The key inputs in the argument are: (1) The arc-descent properties of S ↦ S_perfd, especially Corollary 8.12. (2) André's lemma (Theorem 7.14).' Atlas stages mentioning perfectoidization: Q2, Q4, P8, S2, PR.2, E5 only, all semiperfectoid. No PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22.review.json exists; the reverse edges its routes would need (Q4→P0, Q4→P3, Q3/Q4→Q2) each close a cycle.
findings.fix: Add a late stage PerfectoidQuotients:Q5 'Perfectoidization of integral algebras and J-almost purity' (BS22 §8.2 Cor. 8.11–8.14, §10.1 Def. 10.1–Lemma 10.5, §10.2 Thms 10.9, 10.11 and Lemma 10.12), requiring Q3, Q4, PR.2 and the arc-topology roadmap (BS22 8.10, already routed there). Add edges Q5→P8, Q5→S4, Q5→S2 (acyclic). Rewrite P8's Hodge-type paragraph to follow HJ Lemmas 5.9–5.10, and add Hansen, 'Quotients of adic spaces' (HJ Thm 5.8 uses it) to P8's sources. At the BS22 review, route its items /52, /60, /61 to Q5.

findings.evidence: D6: 'Construct Spd ℤ_p by marked untilts … Construct Spd(A,A⁺) for a Tate ℤ_p-pair … Distinguish a Tate pair from an arbitrary formal base such as (ℤ_p,ℤ_p)' and 'define X^♢ for analytic adic spaces'. Consider the presheaf X♦ …', Lemma 18.1.1 ('the presheaf X♦ is a v-sheaf'), Lemma 18.1.2, Prop. 18.2.2 ('|X♦|→|X| … surjective'). FS arXiv:2102.13459 Prop. II.1.2 and Def. VI.1.1. findings.fix: Add a DiamondsAndVStacks sub-stage D6:pre-adic with the construction of SW §§18.1–18.2: X^♢ for any pre-adic space over Spa ℤ_p, Lemma 18.1.1 (via ECD 15.1(i) and D2's v-descent of O⁺), Prop. 18.2.2 and Lemma 18.1.2. Tests: Spd O_E, (Spd O_E)^d, Spd O_C, Spd(R,R), Spd(R⁺,R⁺) and Spf; comparison maps with L1's integral conventions. D6 is already an ancestor of RF0:integral-Y, RF2:integral-divisors, GS0 and GS1, so no new atlas edge is needed. findings.where: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:comparison vs PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S6
findings.claim: The general Hodge–Tate morphism on the toroidal tower diamond, with its Levi-torsor pullback (Boxer–Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory, Thm 4.4.40), is planned in two layers. No accepted restructuring assigns an owner: RS-05 keeps S6, but HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups is not in its family and none of its owners entries covers this theorem.
findings.evidence: T6:comparison: 'Apply this to the toroidal tower in diamonds, giving the general Hodge–Tate map and coefficient pullback statement of Boxer–Pilloni Theorem 4.4.40.' S6: 'For an arbitrary datum, construct the Hodge–Tate map from the toroidal tower diamond and the canonical Levi-torsor pullback isomorphism via Boxer–Pilloni Theorem 4.4.40.' RS-05 layers[S6]: 'keep … Retain general toroidal diamond Hodge-Tate morphisms and their logarithmic comparison input'. RS-05's roadmaps list has 9 members, without HodgeTate, and its 62 owners have no Hodge–Tate map entry. Boxer–Pilloni arXiv:2110.10251v1 p. 78: 4.4.38 and the text before Thm 4.4.40 give the finite-level log association and M_HT = M_dR on S^tor_{K,Σ}; Thm 4.4.40 concerns the limit S^{tor,◇}_{K^p,Σ}. T6:comparison has no ancestor in PerfectoidShimuraVarieties, where the towers are built, while S6 already requires T6.
findings.fix: Add an owners entry {target 'General-datum toroidal-tower π^tor_HT and Levi-torsor pullback (BP Thm 4.4.40)', owner PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S6, formerly [HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:comparison]}. Narrow T6:comparison, the T6 parent text and the roadmap summary to the finite-level logarithmic content (log period sheaves, log Poincaré lemma, log Riemann–Hilbert, W_p⊗OB_dR,log ≅ W_dR⊗OB_dR,log, the HT filtration and M_HT = M_dR at finite level, BP 4.4.38–4.4.39), exported to S6 through the existing T6→S6 edge.

findings.where: PerfectoidSpaces:P1 nodes P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi and P1/deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras; RS-05 narrowing of P0
findings.claim: The accepted decomposition proves the tilting equivalence by Scholze 2012's field-only route: the almost cotangent complex and Gabber–Ramero almost deformation theory. RS-05 therefore makes P0 build the almost cotangent/deformation extension. That work is unnecessary. P1 already plans ECD 3.14–3.17, the classification of untilts with its converse construction, and in the literature this implies the tilting equivalence (ECD 3.13) directly in the general Tate-ring setting P1 demands, with no cotangent complex. Scholze 2012's route proves only the field case, which is the gap the decomposition records.
findings.evidence: P1: 'Prove classification of marked untilts by primitive degree-one ideals, including the converse construction … (ECD 3.14–3.17) … Construct the equivalence of perfectoid algebras over a fixed perfectoid ring and over its tilt'. Node P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt: 'Sch12 proves the equivalence over a perfectoid base field K; the Tate-ring version (ECD 3.13) is not proved in either source read here'. Decomposition gap: 'the almost-context versions (GR §2.5, §3.2) have no supplier stage'. RS-05 P0 keeps: 'Add the almost-context cotangent/deformation extension required by the accepted P1 nodes, using DD.0 classical cotangent theory'. Scholze–Weinstein Berkeley §6.2: 'From here, one gets the following theorem, which implies Theorem 6.2.7. Theorem 6.2.11 ([KL15], [Fon13]). There is an equivalence of categories between: 1. Perfectoid Tate-Huber pairs (S,S⁺) 2. Triples (R,R⁺,J) …'. Kedlaya–Liu arXiv:1301.0792v5 Thm 3.6.5 (p. 88).
findings.fix: In P1, derive ECD 3.13 as a corollary of 3.17 (untilt a perfectoid R♭-algebra T as W(T⁺)/J·W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ]] with J = ker θ_R). Drop the two Scholze 2012 deformation nodes or mark them optional alternatives. Remove from RS-05's P0 narrowing the almost-context cotangent/deformation extension and the DD.0 → P0/P1/P2/P3/P7 links added only for it, keeping any almost-étale lifting that P0 or P3 need for their own results as a separate question for P3.

findings.where: Stage edge PerfectoidQuotients:Q4 → AdicEtaleGeometry:A3
findings.claim: A3 lists Q4 among its inputs, but the proof A3 implements (ECD Prop. 6.4(iv)) works in characteristic p. It uses Huber 1.7.1, Kedlaya–Liu's pseudocoherent sheaves and FS IV.4.19, which concerns Zariski-closed immersions of sousperfectoid spaces in FS's surjectivity sense. It does not use ECD 5.8 or BS22 7.4 (prismatic perfectoidization), and the transfer by tilting concerns the étale map, which P3 supplies. The single edge makes derived prismatic cohomology an ancestor of every diamond: with the accepted RS links applied, deleting it removes 17 stages from D1's ancestry (PR.0–PR.2, the seven Q stages, CR.0–CR.2, DD.1, DD.2, DD.5, E4).
findings.evidence: A3: 'Inputs: P2–P5 and Q4, plus A0–A2 … Prove the following analytic input in characteristic p, then transfer by tilting' (the text cites no use of Q4). ECD (Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, 2026 manuscript), proof of Prop. 6.4(iv): 'For essential surjectivity, we can work in characteristic p, where it follows from [Hub96, Proposition 1.7.1], which holds for affinoid perfectoid spaces of characteristic p by using the theory of pseudocoherent sheaves of Kedlaya–Liu, [KL16]. More precisely, … one can find a Zariski closed immersion of sousperfectoid adic spaces Y ↪ B^n_X … see [FS26, Proposition IV.4.19]'. ECD Thm 5.8 ('a Zariski closed immersion … is strongly Zariski closed. Proof. This follows from [BS22, Theorem 7.4, Remark 7.5]') concerns perfectoid spaces and is not invoked in 6.4(iv). FS Prop. IV.4.19 / Def. IV.4.20 use no BS22 input. Scholze, torsion paper (Annals 182, 2015), Lemma II.2.5, for characteristic p: 'the map R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective'.
findings.fix: Delete Q4 → A3 and remove Q4 from A3's Inputs line. If a characteristic-p Zariski-closed statement is needed, have P4 prove it elementarily (torsion paper Lemma II.2.5, extended to perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p) and add P4 → A3. Keep P3 → A3 for the tilting transfer. Q4 then remains an input only of P8, S2, S4 and PR.4.

findings.where: DiamondsAndVStacks:D5 vs TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0
findings.claim: Two layers plan the Berkovich spectrum M(R) of bounded multiplicative seminorms and the theorem that |Spa(A,A⁺)| → M(A) is the maximal Hausdorff quotient: D5 for affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD 13.7–13.11) and TB.0 for Banach and strictly affinoid algebras. There is no edge between them and no restructuring covers the pair.
findings.evidence: D5: 'Construct the Berkovich/maximal-Hausdorff quotient functor'. TB.0: 'Construct the Berkovich spectrum of a Banach algebra from bounded multiplicative seminorms … Compare a strictly affinoid algebra with its Huber adic spectrum by rank-one points/maximal generalizations … the correct quotient topology'. ECD Def. 13.7 ('|X|^B … all multiplicative bounded nonarchimedean seminorms') and Prop. 13.9 ('identifying |X|^B as the maximal Hausdorff quotient of |X|'). Accepted routes into TB.0: SCHOLZE-26/4 and ZAVYALOV-25/134. Mathlib carriers only: MulRingSeminorm (RingSeminorm.lean:62), T2Quotient (Hausdorff.lean:413).
findings.fix: Make an early TB.0:spectrum (inputs LI.0 and Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 2 only) the single owner of M(R) for Banach and complete Tate rings and of the maximal-Hausdorff theorem for complete Tate Huber pairs, built on MulRingSeminorm and T2Quotient. Narrow D5 to ECD 13.10–13.13, the extension to small v-sheaves, and add TB.0:spectrum → D5 (acyclic).

BHATT-18 route 9 brief: 'The first final theorem is: every finite injective map A0→B0 of Noetherian commutative rings with A0 regular admits an A0-linear retraction'; item BHATT-18/direct-summand is 'missing', planned none. No PAPER-BHATT-18.review.json exists.
findings.fix: For REV-PAPER-BHATT-18: mark BHATT-18/direct-summand as planned in DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay and make it a source route there; restrict RegularRingSplittings to Bhatt's derived splitting theorem (Thms 1.2, 6.1), importing the direct-summand roadmap's purity/retraction prefix and P7's towers.

findings.where: PerfectoidSpaces:P7 and its decomposition gap 'Frobenius-controlled towers'
findings.claim: P7's source for the Frobenius-lift perfectoid criterion, 'torsion paper II.1–II.2' (the gap says 'Lemma II.2.1 / Cor. II.2.3 range'), points to the wrong sections, 'Constructing formal models from affinoid covers' and 'Closed Embeddings of perfectoid spaces'. The argument is in §III.2.3, with tilde-limit uniqueness from Scholze–Weinstein, Moduli of p-divisible groups §2.4.
findings.evidence: Scholze, torsion paper (Annals 182, 2015), Cor. III.2.19 (pp. 989–990): 'using that the transition maps R_m/p^{1−ε} → R_{m+1}/p^{1−ε} agree with the relative Frobenius map, we find that (absolute) Frobenius induces an isomorphism R∞/p^{(1−ε)/p} ≅ R∞/p^{1−ε}. Thus … R∞^a is a perfectoid …; cf. [55, Def. 2.4.1, Prop. 2.4.2] and, for uniqueness, cf. [55, Prop. 2.4.5].'
findings.fix: Replace the P7 locator with 'torsion paper §III.2.3, Def. III.2.18 – Cor. III.2.19; Scholze–Weinstein (Moduli of p-divisible groups) Def. 2.4.1, Prop. 2.4.2 and 2.4.5', and correct the decomposition gap.

findings.where: Stage edge RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y → VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0
findings.claim: VB0 (isocrystals and Dieudonné–Manin, semilinear algebra) needs only W_{O_E}(F̄_q) from RF0's raw ramified-Witt construction. The atlas cannot point at that construction, because the RF0 aggregate depends on its own children, so VB0 is wired to the integral period space and inherits P1–P4, AdicSpacesPartII R0–R3/R5 and A3. The same unaddressable prefix is the target of the ZHU-17/3 and BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/15 routes, whose consumer is GS0:Witt-geometry.
findings.evidence: VB0 requires ['RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y', 'UPSTREAM:LocalFieldsRamification']; its decomposition node works over 'L = W_{O_E}(F_q-bar)' with no 𝒴_S. RS-15 (accepted), VB0: 'the actual bundle-functor comparison is performed only after the VB1 functor exists'. RF0 requires RF0:annuli and RF0:integral-Y; the decomposition gap notes 'the ramified Witt construction precedes the integral period space'.
findings.fix: Split node RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property into its own stage (e.g. RF0:ramified-Witt) with inputs LocalFieldsRamification and Mathlib WittVector only, add edges from it to RF0:integral-Y, VB0 and GS0:Witt-geometry, delete RF0:integral-Y → VB0, and retarget the ZHU-17/3 and BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/15 routes.
